h1: The 5 Best Greenworks Leaf Blowers of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Greenworks Leaf Blowers: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: five cordless Greenworks leaf blowers across 40V, 60V and 80V platforms, compared by airflow in CFM and price bucket.
summary: The Greenworks 80V at 770 CFM is the best Greenworks leaf blower for large yards, and the 80V at 730 CFM delivers nearly the same airflow for a lower price. The 40V 730 CFM suits owners of existing 40V batteries. The 500 CFM 40V is a starter blower for small yards.
intro: Greenworks sells nearly identical blowers across 40V, 60V and 80V batteries, and the number of volts on the box tells you surprisingly little about how hard the air blows. In this group a 40V model matches an 80V one on airflow, which catches buyers who assume that bigger voltage means more power.

We reviewed five cordless Greenworks blowers and ranked them by listed CFM and price bucket. Our facts do not include runtime, weight or box contents, so check the live listing for those details, especially whether a battery and charger are included. Treat voltage as a platform question, to be answered by the batteries you already own.

products.name: Greenworks 80V Electric Leaf Blower (770 CFM)
products.verdict: The highest airflow in the group at 770 CFM.
products.description:
The Greenworks 80V Electric Leaf Blower at 770 CFM is a cordless unit in the $200 to $500 bucket, with the highest airflow in this ranking.

It takes first place because nothing else here moves more air. The reason the lead is slim is the 730 CFM 80V model just below it, which gives up only 40 CFM and costs a full bucket less. If you clear heavy autumn piles from a big lot every week, those extra cubic feet are worth having, and the 80V platform suits larger properties.

Buy it for large yards and deep leaf cover. Skip it if you have a small yard. The listing gives no runtime or weight, so check those before you pay the premium, and confirm whether a battery comes in the box.
products.idealFor: Large yards and heavy leaf cleanup.

products.name: Greenworks 80V Electric Leaf Blower (730 CFM)
products.verdict: 730 CFM from a lower price bucket than the leader.
products.description:
The 80V 730 CFM Greenworks is also cordless, sits in the $100 to $200 bucket and moves just 40 CFM less than the leader.

Second place is the result of a value argument. The difference between 730 and 770 CFM is small enough to be unnoticeable to most people, while the price drops by a bucket. Nothing else in the group offers as much air per dollar, which is why this model is the one many buyers should actually order.

Buy it if you want near-top airflow without paying top dollar, particularly for a big yard. Skip it if you must have every last CFM. Because the listing does not describe the box contents, confirm whether you need to purchase batteries and a charger separately, as that can shift the real cost.
products.idealFor: Big yards on a smaller budget.

products.name: Greenworks 40V Electric Leaf Blower (730 CFM)
products.verdict: A 40V model matching the 80V airflow, in a higher bucket.
products.description:
The 40V Greenworks at 730 CFM matches the 80V model's airflow on a smaller battery platform, in the $200 to $500 bucket.

It lands third because it costs more than the cheaper 80V twin for the same listed airflow. The reason to choose it is the platform: if you already own 40V batteries from a Greenworks mower or trimmer, a bare blower may save you considerable money overall, and 730 CFM is strong enough for most residential leaf clearing.

Buy it if you already have 40V batteries and chargers. Skip it if you are starting from nothing, since the 80V model at 730 CFM costs a bucket less. Runtime is not listed in our facts, so confirm it for the battery you already have before treating this as a guaranteed fit.

products.name: Greenworks 60V Electric Leaf Blower (610 CFM)
products.description:
The 60V Greenworks lists 610 CFM, cordless, in the $200 to $500 bucket.

Fourth place follows from a poor combination: less airflow than the 730 and 770 CFM models while costing more than the 80V 730 CFM version. The 60V platform is its only distinguishing trait, and it matters solely if you own the batteries already. For everyone else, the same money or less buys noticeably more air elsewhere in the range.

Buy it if you have Greenworks 60V tools and want a blower that uses the same packs. Skip it if you are shopping on airflow per dollar. Verify what is included in the box, since a bare tool and a full kit are very different purchases, and the listing here does not say which one you receive.
products.skipIf: You want the best airflow per dollar.

products.name: Greenworks 40V Cordless Leaf Blower (500 CFM)
products.verdict: 500 CFM at a lower price for small yards.
products.description:
The 40V Greenworks at 500 CFM is a cordless starter blower in the $100 to $200 bucket, the lowest airflow of the five.

It finishes last on raw power, but it shares a price bucket with the 80V 730 CFM model, which is the real problem: for a similar spend, that model moves far more air. This one earns a place only by suiting small, simple jobs such as clearing a patio, a driveway or a thin layer of leaves from a modest lawn.

Buy it for a small yard where heavy leaf piles are not an issue. Skip it if you clear large areas or wet leaves, because 500 CFM will feel underpowered. If you own 40V batteries already, it may be the cheapest way to add a blower to the set.

whatMatters.detail: CFM stands for cubic feet of air per minute, a rough gauge of how large a leaf pile the machine can push. Find the number in the title or bullets. This group runs from 500 CFM on the 40V starter to 770 CFM on the top 80V blower.

Voltage names the battery platform. Greenworks 40V, 60V and 80V packs do not swap, so match the blower to batteries you already own. Do not assume higher volts mean more air. The 40V 730 CFM and the 80V 730 CFM models list identical airflow.

Price buckets here range from $100 to $200 up to $200 to $500, and the same airflow appears in both. Compare CFM first, then pay extra only for a stated reason such as an existing battery platform. The 730 CFM 80V model is in the lower bucket, while the 40V 730 CFM is in the higher.

Some listings include a battery and charger, others sell the tool alone. The battery is often the most expensive part, so it changes the real price. Read the box contents line on each listing. Our facts do not say what ships with these Greenworks blowers, so confirm before buying.

Yard size should set your airflow target. A small patio needs far less air than an acre of oaks, and buying too much blower wastes money. Match CFM to your biggest cleanup job. The 500 CFM model suits small spaces, while the 730 and 770 CFM models suit big properties.

faq.q: Does higher voltage mean more airflow?
faq.a: No. The 40V Greenworks at 730 CFM matches the airflow of the 80V 730 CFM model, so volts mainly identify the battery platform. Compare CFM and price bucket, then match the voltage to batteries you own.

faq.q: What is the most common mistake?
faq.a: Buying by voltage alone. An 80V blower is not automatically stronger than a 40V one in this group. Look at the CFM figure and the price bucket first, and only then choose a platform.

faq.q: Is the 770 CFM model worth it over the 730?
faq.a: Only for the biggest yards. The 770 CFM 80V model moves 40 CFM more than the 730 CFM version, but it sits in the $200 to $500 bucket while the 730 is in the $100 to $200 bucket.

faq.q: Do batteries come in the box?
faq.a: Our facts do not say, so check each listing. Whether a battery and charger come with the 80V 770 CFM or any other Greenworks blower makes a large difference to the true cost.

faq.q: How do I maintain a cordless blower?
faq.a: Clean the air intake of leaves and debris after each use, and store the battery as the manual advises. Avoid leaving it in extreme heat or cold, and charge it before long storage.

faq.q: Can I use 40V batteries in an 80V blower?
faq.a: No. Battery platforms differ, so 40V packs do not fit an 80V tool. Match the voltage on the blower to batteries you own, such as 40V for the 500 CFM model.

finalTake: For a large yard, the Greenworks 80V at 730 CFM is the smart buy, offering almost the same airflow as the 770 CFM leader for a bucket less. Choose the 770 CFM version if you want every last bit of air, and the 40V models only if you already own 40V batteries. Pick by CFM and price first, then match the platform.
